title: A lisse sheaf on a normal open has constructible direct image
statement:
Let $X$ be integral of finite type over a field, let
$k:V\hookrightarrow X$ be a nonempty
normal open,
and let $L$ be a finite locally constant module sheaf
over a finite ring. Then the
direct image $k_*L$
is constructible.

proof.text: Write $\Lambda$ for the finite commutative coefficient ring (as in the constructibility convention). The field is Noetherian, since its only ideals are zero and the whole field. Thus $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Its open $V$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]; in particular it is quasi-compact. In an affine finite-type chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $X$, the principal opens $D(f)$ contained in $V$ cover its intersection with $V$. Their rings $A_f=A[t]/(ft-1)$ are finite-type algebras over the field. Quasi-compactness of $V$ selects finitely many such opens, proving that $V$ is of finite type over the field. Choose a finite etale surjective $p:P\to V$ and finite modules trivializing $p^*L$ on its connected components by [fin2-lem-lisse-trivialized-finite-etale]. A finite algebra is of finite type (its module generators also generate it as an algebra), so $P$ is of finite type over the field and is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Apply [lem-fin-etale-normal-components] to $P\to V$: write $P=\coprod_{a=1}^r P_a$ with $P_a$ nonempty open-and-closed normal integral schemes. They are the connected components, so $p^*L|_{P_a}\cong\underline{M_a}$ for finite $\Lambda$-modules $M_a$. The restrictions $p_a:P_a\to V$ remain finite etale: on an affine base, restriction to an open-and-closed component is passage to an idempotent factor of the finite algebra.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: choose the trivializing cover and its components

proof.text: Let $L_{\mathrm{ab}}$ denote the underlying abelian sheaf. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact](1) and [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-inverse-image-comparison], the underlying morphism of the module adjunction unit $L\to p_*p^*L$ is the abelian adjunction unit, using its canonical inverse-image comparison. For a geometric point $\bar v$ of $V$, [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] identifies its target with $\prod_{\bar z\in P_{\bar v}}(p^{-1}L_{\mathrm{ab}})_{\bar z}$. The germ compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] identifies every component of the unit with the identity on $(L_{\mathrm{ab}})_{\bar v}$. Hence the stalk map is $m\mapsto(m)_{\bar z}$. The fibre is nonempty because $p$ is surjective, so this map is injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-detect-mono] the underlying abelian unit is monic. It is therefore also monic as a module morphism: equality of module morphisms can be tested after forgetting the action.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: the adjunction unit is a stalkwise diagonal injection

proof.text: Each $p_a$ is surjective. Indeed its nonempty image is open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map] and closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]; the nonempty open $V$ of the integral $X$ is irreducible, so its only nonempty open-and-closed subset is $V$. Put $K=k(X)=k(V)$. The generic fibre of $p_a$ is a nonzero finite-dimensional domain over $K$: over a nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq V$, write its inverse image as $\operatorname{Spec}D$. This inverse image is nonempty by surjectivity and is an open of the integral $P_a$, so $D$ is a domain. The ring map $B\to D$ is injective: surjectivity on spectra implies its kernel is contained in every prime ideal of $B$, hence in the nilradical; $B$ is a domain because $V$ is integral, so this nilradical is zero. Also $D$ is finite over $B$. Thus $(B\setminus\{0\})^{-1}D$ is a nonzero finite-dimensional domain over $K=\operatorname{Frac}B$. Every nonzero element of a finite-dimensional domain over a field is invertible, because multiplication by it is an injective endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space and hence surjective. Thus this generic fibre is the field $K_a=k(P_a)$ and $K_a/K$ is finite.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: the function fields used to extend the connected covers

proof.text: Let $g_a:Y_a\to X$ be the normalization in $K_a$ of [def-fin-normalization-extension]. By [lem-fin-normalization-extends-cover] its restriction over $V$ is $p_a:P_a\to V$; hence $P_a=g_a^{-1}(V)$ is a nonempty open subscheme of $Y_a$, with inclusion $v_a$, and $g_av_a=kp_a$. The finite-extension hypothesis needed by [lem-fin-normalization-extension-finite] holds by step 3, so $g_a$ is finite. To justify normality independently of the proof of the cover-extension node, first $X$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-in-residue-field-extension] at its generic point with residue field $K$ and extension $K_a$: its specified normalization is normal integral with function field $K_a$, and is the same normalization just defined (both have the integral closure of each affine coordinate ring in $K_a$). Finally $Y_a$ is of finite type over the field, since $g_a$ is finite, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $Y_a$ Noetherian.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: extend each component by finite normal integral normalization

proof.text:
Apply [lem-fin-normal-constant-open-image] to the Noetherian normal integral $Y_a$, its nonempty open $v_a:P_a\hookrightarrow Y_a$, and the finite module $M_a$. It gives $v_{a,*}\underline{M_a}\cong\underline{M_a}_{Y_a}$. The section formula of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] then gives $(kp_a)_*\underline{M_a}\cong g_{a,*}\underline{M_a}_{Y_a}$: both compositions of direct images evaluate on an etale object by successive fibre products, canonically the fibre product with the composite map. All maps respect $\Lambda$-actions. Applying the left-exact functor $k_*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact] to step 2 and using the sheaf axiom on the finite disjoint union $P=\coprod_aP_a$ now gives a monomorphism
$$k_*L\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow\prod_a g_{a,*}\underline{M_a}_{Y_a}.$$
For the disjoint union $Y=\coprod_aY_a$, define $E$ on an etale object $W\to Y$ by $E(W)=\prod_a\underline{M_a}_{Y_a}(W\times_Y Y_a)$, with componentwise restriction and module operations. Each component satisfies the sheaf condition, so this formula defines a module sheaf; restricting to $Y_a$ gives $\underline{M_a}$, since the other fibre products are empty and a module sheaf has zero sections on the empty scheme. Let $g:Y\to X$ restrict to $g_a$. On every etale object, sections on this disjoint union are the corresponding finite product, so the right hand side is $g_*E$. The morphism $g$ is finite: above an affine $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X$ it is the spectrum of the finite product of the finite $B$-algebras for the $g_a$; embed each component algebra's finite module generating set in its factor, with zero in all other factors; the union of these embedded sets generates the product as a $B$-module.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: constant open image, composition, and the finite product of finite direct images

proof.text: The finite clopen partition $Y=\coprod_aY_a$ and the componentwise constant finite module restrictions define the sheaf $E$ in step 5. The new node [lem-fin-normal-clopen-constructible-module] states that this partition is a constructibility stratification, so $E$ is constructible.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: constructibility of the finite direct images; module-valued version

proof.text: The clopen etale cover $\{Y_a\to Y\}$ and the finite constant module restrictions of step 5 satisfy (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values]. Its last assertion identifies every algebraically closed module stalk of $E$ with the corresponding finite $M_a$. The Mathlib leaf [lem-fin-normal-underlying-stalk-finite] identifies its underlying set with the set-sheaf stalk; hence those set stalks are finite.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: constructibility of the finite direct images; module-valued version

proof.text: Apply [lem-galois-finite-stalks-comparison] to the underlying set sheaf of $E$, whose algebraically closed stalks are finite by step 7. Its set stalks are therefore finite at every separably closed point. The bijection at these points supplied by [lem-fin-normal-underlying-stalk-finite] transfers this finiteness to the underlying sets of the module stalks, as required by the next theorem.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: constructibility of the finite direct images; module-valued version

proof.text: The morphism $g:Y\to X$ is finite by step 5. By step 6, $E$ is constructible in the coefficient-category sense [def-constructible-constructible], and by step 8 all its separably closed module stalks are finite. The target $X$ is Noetherian by step 1. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-finite-stalk-module] applies and gives constructibility of $g_*E$ in the coefficient-category sense [def-constructible-constructible]. Since $\Lambda$ is finite, [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison] converts this into constructibility of $g_*E$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], the hypothesis of the subobject theorem used in step 10.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: constructibility of the finite direct images; module-valued version

proof.text: The monomorphism $k_*L\hookrightarrow g_*E$ from step 5 has constructible target by step 9. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-subobjects-noetherian], with the Noetherian scheme $X$ and the given finite commutative ring $\Lambda$, to conclude that $k_*L$ is constructible.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: apply the Noetherian subobject theorem

proof_origin.place: Proof, both paragraphs; expanded hypotheses, unit compatibility, and module-valued finite-pushforward argument

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q39-e538a2a02 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, both new nodes, the statements of all cited nodes, the master and main-20261015 blueprint proof, the unit sk-prop-a1-kummer, and the Mathlib source (Point/Basic.lean:354 sheafFiberCompIso, EtalePoint.lean:33/64 pointSmallEtale with IsSepClosed, ModuleCat FilteredColimits.lean:202). Steps 1-5 are byte-identical to the base proof. I reread them and every hypothesis holds: P is Noetherian, V is normal integral, P_a is connected finite etale, K_a/K is finite, Y_a is Noetherian, normal and integral, g is finite. New steps 6-8 are correct. Step 7 uses the finite-locally-constant-module-values (1) clause and its 'moreover' clause with the clopen cover. Step 8 goes through the Galois algebraically-closed to separably-closed comparison and then the leaf, which gives exactly the finite-stalk hypothesis that the finite-pushforward node needs. One fault (C1/C4, already present in the old step 6): finite-pushforward-finite-stalk-module concludes IsConstructibleSheaf, but the subobject theorem in step 10 needs IsConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf, and the comparison node between them was not cited. Fixed step 9 to cite lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison (Λ is finite) and def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf; recomputed proof_deps; added a split_report.tool_uses entry. There is no cycle. The clopen child is true: clopen sets are retrocompact and so constructible; restricting along the open immersion gives the constant M_a. I tested it with an empty Y, an empty Y_a, zero modules and the zero ring. It is not a restatement of the parent, and the DAG search found no duplicate. The stalk child is a valid one-line Mathlib specialization with no duplicate in the DAG. Its id mentions 'finite' but the statement has no finiteness clause; that is cosmetic only. Accepted tool uses: the existing split_report list plus the comparison node. Replacing the blueprint's abelian lem-fin-finite-constant-pushforward with the module-valued theorem is accepted.
